definitions.explanation: Indicates that something is taken or used in its entirety, without being divided, peeled, or reduced.

examples.japanese: ⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{丸|まる}ごと⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{丸|まる}ごと⟦{一冊|いっさつ}→一冊：23149_issatsu⟧⟦{読|よ}んだ→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I read this entire book cover to cover.

examples.japanese: ⟦{島|しま}→島：00885_shima⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{丸|まる}ごと⟦ホテル→ホテル：01027_hoteru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発表|はっぴょう}→発表：03562_happyou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A plan to turn the whole island into a hotel was announced.

notes:
USAGE:
{丸|まる}ごと emphasizes completeness — nothing is left out, removed, or divided. It often implies something impressive or surprising about the scale or thoroughness.

Often written in hiragana as まるごと, though the kanji form {丸|まる}ごと is also common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸|まる}ごと⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat whole
- {丸|まる}ごと⟦{一冊|いっさつ}→一冊：23149_issatsu⟧: an entire volume
- {丸|まる}ごと⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use entirely
- {丸|まる}ごと⟦{飲|の}み{込|こ}む→飲み込む：04403_nomikomu⟧: to swallow whole

SIMILAR WORDS:
{丸|まる}ごと vs ⟦そのまま→そのまま：03322_sonomama⟧: {丸|まる}ごと focuses on entirety (the whole thing), while ⟦そのまま→そのまま：03322_sonomama⟧ focuses on leaving something in its current state (as is).
